concepts.def: Contracting cloud of gas and dust accreting mass; precursor to a main-sequence star.
Minimum mass of a gas cloud needed for gravitational collapse to overcome thermal pressure.
Balance between inward gravity and outward pressure; stable stars maintain this state.
Hydrogen fusion catalysed by carbon, nitrogen, oxygen; dominant in stars >1.3 solar masses.
Direct proton-proton fusion to helium; dominant in stars below ~1.3 solar masses (incl. Sun).
For main-sequence stars: L is proportional to M to the power ~3.5; massive stars are vastly more luminous.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Stellar Evolution — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Stellar Evolution brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Stellar Evolution.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which dominates fusion in the Sun?
options: CNO cycle
Triple-alpha
p-p chain
s-process

mcqs.q: Balance of gravity and pressure is called?
options: Adiabatic equilibrium
Hydrostatic equilibrium
Thermal equilibrium
Free fall

mcqs.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
options: It is the largest stage of a star's life.
Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.
It is the hottest stage.
It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.

mcqs.q: What determines whether a star becomes a white dwarf or a neutron star?
options: Its mass - low/medium mass becomes a white dwarf; massive stars produce neutron stars or black holes.
Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.
Its colour during its main sequence phase.
Whether it has planets.

mcqs.q: Why are Type Ia supernovae used as 'standard candles'?
options: Because they happen at regular time intervals.
They have nearly uniform peak brightness, so their apparent brightness reveals distance.
It is the hottest stage.
Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mass-luminosity relation”?
options: Direct proton-proton fusion to helium; dominant in stars below ~1.3 solar masses (incl. Sun).
For main-sequence stars: L is proportional to M to the power ~3.5; massive stars are vastly more luminous.
Minimum mass of a gas cloud needed for gravitational collapse to overcome thermal pressure.
Hydrogen fusion catalysed by carbon, nitrogen, oxygen; dominant in stars >1.3 solar masses.
